name: Databox
summary: Centralized KPI dashboards. Pull data from all your software tools into one clean interface to monitor your business health. A free Skills Marketplace adds guided analyses on top: the paid-ads skill standardizes every ad channel into one efficiency table with CPA gauges against your own targets, judged per funnel role. A native MCP server (mcp.databox.com) puts those metrics inside ChatGPT or Claude, where you can ingest data and query it in plain language. It is listed on the Business plan, and its queries spend from the same monthly AI-credit pool as Genie.
best_for: SMBs and agencies that want clean KPI dashboards from 130+ one-click integrations without building them by hand
skip_if: you only need a few sources for one person: since November 2026 there is no free plan and the self-serve Business plan is $399 a month billed annually, so a free tool like Looker Studio fits better, as it does if you want deep custom data modelling
honest_knock: The pricing has moved upmarket. On 12 November 2026 the page sold one self-serve plan, Business, at $399 a month billed annually ($499 monthly) for up to 10 users, 30 data sources and 1,500 AI credits a month. The free plan and the cheaper Analyst, Team Core and Team Scale tiers we read in October are gone, so a solo user or a small team now pays the same entry price as a ten-person one. Only the Agency plan sells capacity piecemeal, from $79 a month plus $20 account packs. AI credits are a shared monthly pool for Genie and the MCP server, and 15-minute sync, once part of the top plan, is now a $14 per-source add-on on top of the subscription. Power users may also find the custom-metric and data-modelling depth limited next to a full BI tool.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-12 on their own pricing page) NEW: the page now sells one self-serve plan, Business, at $399 a month billed annually ($4,788 a year) or $499 billed monthly, with up to 10 users, up to 30 data sources, 1,500 AI credits a month and email support. Agency is $79 a month billed annually plus $20 a month per account pack (1 account, 5 data sources, 50 AI credits); add-ons are unchanged at $200, $80, $40, $160 and $14 per source (annual rates). A done-for-you Custom service starts from $15,000. The page no longer shows a Free plan, Analyst, Team Core or Team Scale, and its FAQ answers 'Do you offer a free plan?' with 'No. Every account starts with a 14-day trial of the Platform plan instead, with no credit card required.' The page states no spreadsheet limit. OLD READING (re-verified 2026-10-02, 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-20, read on their own pricing page): Databox renamed and repriced its whole ladder since our August reading, so the Analyst/Pro/Growth tiers we described are gone. Free is $0 forever: 1 user, 3 data sources, 1 dashboard, 10 custom metrics, 50 AI credits a month, daily sync. Billed annually: Analyst $71/mo (1 user, 5 sources, unlimited dashboards and reports, 150 credits, hourly sync), Team Core $199/mo (3 users, 10 sources, 500 credits), Team Scale $319/mo (10 users, 30 sources, 1,000 credits, sub-accounts) and Agency from $79/mo (unlimited users, 4 clients, 20 sources, 300 credits), plus a quoted Custom tier. Monthly, Analyst reads $89 and the others $249, $399 and from $99; annual billing is 20% off. Databox states it does not charge per seat. Extra data sources no longer carry a per-source fee: each plan includes a fixed number and more means moving up a tier, except on Agency, which adds client packs of 1 client, 5 sources and 50 credits for $20/mo annually ($25 monthly). Add-ons are priced separately: branding and white-labeling $200/mo, advanced security management $80/mo, OKRs $160/mo, fiscal calendar $40/mo, 15-minute sync $14/mo per source, and flexible AI credit top-ups. Those add-on amounts are the annual-billing rates; on monthly billing the page shows $250 for branding, $100 for security management, $200 for OKRs, $50 for the fiscal calendar and $18 per source for 15-minute sync.

sessions.what: We opened a new Databox account through the 'Get started' button under the Free plan on databox.com/pricing, connected Google Analytics 4 and Google Search Console for our own site, asked Genie two questions about that data, let Genie try to build a dashboard, and read the credit meter under Settings → Billing after every step. One account, one evening, our own traffic data, not a month of team use.
findings: The Free button does not give you Free. The account opened as a 14-day trial of Team Core at $249 a month, billed monthly. Free was listed in the app as a 'Downgrade'. Databox's own FAQ says that if no payment details are added by the end of the trial, syncing stops and reports pause, so anyone who wanted Free has to downgrade by hand before day 14.

The downgrade was blocked until we deleted Databox's own sample data. The message: 'You have 1 connected Spreadsheets, but the Free plan is limited to 0.' That one spreadsheet was the Sample dataset Databox adds at sign-up. Free allows no spreadsheets at all: Excel and Google Sheets both open an 'Upgrade to Analyst' wall at $89 a month, something the pricing page does not say.

Your one free dashboard is already taken. Databox's own Sample Dashboard stays after the downgrade and fills the plan's single dashboard slot. 'Create New Databoard' opened the $89 upgrade wall, and so did the button that would hang the sample dashboard on your own data.

What a Genie question costs: 3.7 credits for a simple one ('which pages got the most views in August'), 3.8 for a heavier week-by-week comparison. On Free's 50 a month that is about thirteen questions. The onboarding had already spent 1.9 credits by sending our four setup answers to Genie as a first question we never asked, and the app showed 'Buy more to keep Genie running' at 48 left.

Genie spends credits on things the plan will not allow. It offered to build a dashboard, tried three times, reported that Databox 'rejected the request as invalid' without naming the one-dashboard limit, and charged 5.2 credits for nothing. After one hour we had used 14.6 of the month's 50 credits.

Genie's diagnoses need checking. It called a half-finished Search Console connection 'broken' because 'the login expires' (the data manager said 'Unfinished connection'), and it flagged one of our real review URLs as a typo. The traffic figures themselves came back fast and were usefully broken down, including pages counted twice because of query strings.

What held up: connecting a data source cost no credits, the unfinished connection still counted against the three-source limit, and the plan prices inside the app matched the public pricing page ($89 / $249 / $399 monthly; $71 / $199 / $319 billed annually).
sessions.not_tested: We did not add a fourth data source past the limit, did not build our own dashboard after deleting the sample one, and could not check how fresh each source's data is: the app shows sync frequency but no last-synced time.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

vendor_mcp.what: Server at mcp.databox.com/mcp with two core tools: ingest_data and query_dataset_with_ai — push data in, then ask questions about it in plain language. Their affiliate team adds (31 Jul 2026) that one connection reaches the sources already set up in your Databox account — they put that at 130+ — rather than a separate MCP server for every platform.
vendor_mcp.plan: Every paid plan — the feature comparison marks the MCP server as not included on Free. Use is metered: MCP queries draw on the same monthly AI credit pool as their Genie assistant, 500 credits on Analyst, 1,500 on Pro, 4,000 on Growth and custom above. The 14-day free trial runs on the Growth plan. Their affiliate team confirmed the paid-plan requirement to us in writing on 29 Jul 2026.
